body.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}\), the fourth-cumulant construction satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}\|\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}-\Gamma(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(N^{-1/2})\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}d_H(\Theta_{TY}(\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}},\preceq),\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq))=O(N^{-1/2})\), and \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}}P^{\otimes N}\{\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\subseteq C_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(N\).
body.justification: The theorem locates a transparent parametric boundary of the severely ill-posed Fourier class.
body.gap: Miettinen--Taskinen--Nordhausen--Oja derives fourth-moment ICA limits, but not finite-sample whole-fiber coverage for a greatest Gaussian divisor.
body.consumer: Audited literal-Laplace applications can use root-\(N\) uncertainty rather than the conservative logarithmic region.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}\).  For a multi-index \(r=(r_1,\ldots,r_p)\in\mathbb N_0^p\) with \(1\le |r|:=\sum_i r_i\le4\), put \(Z_r=\prod_{i=1}^pX_i^{r_i}\), \(\mu_r=\mathbb E_P Z_r\), and \(\overline Z_r=N^{-1}\sum_{n=1}^N\prod_iX_{ni}^{r_i}\).  Let \(B=\sqrt{V_8}\), and let \(\widehat\mu_r=\operatorname{clip}_{[-B,B]}(\overline Z_r)\), as prescribed by \(\mathrm{def:laplace\mbox{-}region}\).  Since \(|Z_r|\le\|X\|^{|r|}\), the elementary inequality \(z^{2|r|}\le1+z^8\) for \(z\ge0\) and \(|r|\le4\), followed by \(\mathrm{ass:eighth\mbox{-}moment}\), gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P Z_r^2
 \le \mathbb E_P\|X\|^{2|r|}
 \le 1+\mathbb E_P\|X\|^8
 \le 1+M_8=V_8.
\]
Consequently \(|\mu_r|\le(\mathbb E_PZ_r^2)^{1/2}\le B\) by Cauchy--Schwarz.  Projection onto \([-B,B]\) cannot increase distance from the point \(\mu_r\in[-B,B]\), so
\[
 |\widehat\mu_r-\mu_r|\le|\overline Z_r-\mu_r|.
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:iid}\), \(\mathbb E_P(\overline Z_r-\mu_r)^2=N^{-1}\operatorname{Var}_P(Z_r)\le V_8/N\).  Summing over the \(d_4\) multi-indices therefore yields the uniform bound
\[
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|_2^2
 \le \frac{d_4V_8}{N}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Jensen's inequality applied to (1) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|_2
 \le \sqrt{\frac{d_4V_8}{N}},
 \tag{2}
\]
whereas Markov's inequality applied to the squared norm and the definition \(r_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}=\sqrt{d_4V_8/(N\alpha)}\) gives
\[
 P^{\otimes N}\!\left\{\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|_2>r_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}\right\}
 \le \frac{d_4V_8/N}{(r_N^{\mathrm{Lap}})^2}=\alpha.
 \tag{3}
\]

We next identify the value of the moment reconstruction at \(\mu\).  The centered standardized Laplace law has density \(f(h)=2^{-1/2}\exp(-\sqrt2|h|)\).  Symmetry gives mean zero, and direct integration using \(\int_0^\infty h^m e^{-ah}\,dh=m!a^{-(m+1)}\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E H_{\mathrm{Lap}}^2
 =\sqrt2\frac{2!}{(\sqrt2)^3}=1,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E H_{\mathrm{Lap}}^4
 =\sqrt2\frac{4!}{(\sqrt2)^5}=6.
\]
Its fourth cumulant is consequently \(6-3\cdot1^2=3\).  Under \(\mathrm{ass:laplace\mbox{-}source}\), \(U=a^{\mathrm{Lap}}H_{\mathrm{Lap}}\).  The additive model in \(\mathrm{def:laplace\mbox{-}model}\) makes this vector independent of the centered Gaussian component.  Additivity of joint cumulants for independent summands, multilinearity, and the vanishing of Gaussian cumulants of order four therefore imply, for every \(i\in V\),
\[
 \kappa_{TTTT}(X)=3(a_T^{\mathrm{Lap}})^4,
 \qquad
 \kappa_{iTTT}(X)=3a_i^{\mathrm{Lap}}(a_T^{\mathrm{Lap}})^3.
 \tag{4}
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:treatment\mbox{-}loading}\), \(|a_T^{\mathrm{Lap}}|\ge a_{\min}>0\).  Thus (4) gives \(\kappa_{TTTT}(X)\ge3a_{\min}^4>(3/2)a_{\min}^4\), so the positive floor in \(F_{p,M_8,a_{\min}}\) is inactive at \(\mu\), all divisions below have positive denominators, and
\[
 a_T(\mu)=|a_T^{\mathrm{Lap}}|,
 \qquad
 a_i(\mu)=\frac{3a_i^{\mathrm{Lap}}(a_T^{\mathrm{Lap}})^3}
 {3|a_T^{\mathrm{Lap}}|^3}
 =\operatorname{sgn}(a_T^{\mathrm{Lap}})a_i^{\mathrm{Lap}}.
 \tag{5}
\]
In particular, \(a(\mu)a(\mu)^\top=a^{\mathrm{Lap}}(a^{\mathrm{Lap}})^\top\).  Independence and unit variance of \(H_{\mathrm{Lap}}\) give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_P(X)
 =a^{\mathrm{Lap}}(a^{\mathrm{Lap}})^\top+\Gamma(P).
 \tag{6}
\]
Equations (5)--(6), together with \(\mathrm{ass:spectral\mbox{-}lower}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:spectral\mbox{-}upper}\), show that the matrix before spectral clipping equals \(\Gamma(P)\) and already has spectrum in \([\lambda,\Lambda]\).  Hence
\[
 F_{p,M_8,a_{\min}}(\mu)=\Gamma(P).
 \tag{7}
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:laplace\mbox{-}region}\), \(\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}=F_{p,M_8,a_{\min}}(\widehat\mu)\).  Since both \(\mu\) and \(\widehat\mu\) belong to \([-\sqrt{V_8},\sqrt{V_8}]^{d_4}\), \(\mathrm{lem:laplace\mbox{-}global\mbox{-}lipschitz}\) and (7) give, for every sample outcome,
\[
 \|\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}-\Gamma(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C_{\mathrm{Lap}}\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|_2.
 \tag{8}
\]
Combining (2) and (8), then taking the supremum over \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}\), proves the explicit uniform estimate
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}}
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}\|\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}-\Gamma(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C_{\mathrm{Lap}}\sqrt{\frac{d_4V_8}{N}}.
 \tag{9}
\]
No loading-norm bound occurs in (1)--(9).

Spectral clipping ensures that \(\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}\) has spectrum in \([\lambda,\Lambda]\), while the same is true of \(\Gamma(P)\) by the two spectral assumptions.  Therefore \(\mathrm{lem:fiber\mbox{-}lipschitz}\), (8), and (2) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}}
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}
 d_H\!\left(\Theta_{TY}(\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}},\preceq),
             \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\right)\\
 &\hspace{25mm}\le L_\beta C_{\mathrm{Lap}}
 \sqrt{\frac{d_4V_8}{N}}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{10}
\]
This proves both asserted \(O(N^{-1/2})\) conclusions with constants independent of \(P\) and \(N\).

It remains to prove finite-sample whole-fiber coverage, including collision strata.  Define the event
\[
 \mathcal E_N=\left\{\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|_2\le r_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}\right\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal E_N\), (8) and \(\mathrm{lem:fiber\mbox{-}lipschitz}\) give
\[
 d_H\!\left(\Theta_{TY}(\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}},\preceq),
             \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\right)
 \le R_N,
 \qquad
 R_N:=L_\beta C_{\mathrm{Lap}}r_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}.
 \tag{11}
\]
By \(\mathrm{prop:ideal\mbox{-}fiber}\),
\[
 \Theta_{TY}(H,\preceq)=\{\beta_J(H):J\in\mathcal J\}
 \tag{12}
\]
for \(H=\Gamma(P)\) and for \(H=\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}\).  Thus, for every \(\theta\in\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\), the first directed term in the Hausdorff distance in (11) and (12) supply some \(J\in\mathcal J\) such that
\[
 |\theta-\beta_J(\widehat\Gamma_N^{\mathrm{Lap}})|\le R_N.
 \tag{13}
\]
There is no branch matching or separation step in this argument, so (13) remains valid when two or more ideal branches collide exactly.

We finally check that the terminal intersection with \([-\Lambda/\lambda,\Lambda/\lambda]\) in \(C_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}\) cannot delete a true effect.  Write \(S=D\cup J\).  By construction \(T\notin S\).  If \(Y\in S\), the partial covariance formula gives \(\gamma_{YT\cdot S}(\Gamma(P))=0\).  If \(Y\notin S\), the Schur complement of \(\Gamma(P)_{SS}\) is positive definite, so Cauchy--Schwarz for this conditional covariance matrix gives
\[
 |\gamma_{YT\cdot S}(\Gamma(P))|
 \le\sqrt{\gamma_{YY\cdot S}(\Gamma(P))
                 \gamma_{TT\cdot S}(\Gamma(P))}.
\]
The variational formula for a Schur complement and \(\lambda I\preceq\Gamma(P)\preceq\Lambda I\) yield
\[
 \gamma_{TT\cdot S}(\Gamma(P))\ge\lambda,
 \qquad
 \gamma_{YY\cdot S}(\Gamma(P))\le\Gamma(P)_{YY}\le\Lambda.
\]
Therefore, in either case,
\[
 |\beta_J(\Gamma(P))|
 \le\sqrt{\Lambda/\lambda}
 \le\Lambda/\lambda,
 \tag{14}
\]
where the last inequality uses \(0<\lambda<\Lambda\).  Equations (12)--(14) and the definition in \(\mathrm{def:laplace\mbox{-}region}\) imply on \(\mathcal E_N\) that
\[
 \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\subseteq C_N^{\mathrm{Lap}}.
\]
By (3), \(P^{\otimes N}(\mathcal E_N)\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lap}}\); taking the infimum over \(P\) proves the advertised honest coverage for every \(N\).

For completeness, all constructions are measurable.  Empirical raw moments, coordinate projections, cumulant polynomials, the maximum with a positive constant, roots and reciprocal powers on the positive-floor domain, and spectral projection are Borel maps.  Matrix inversion is continuous on matrices bounded below by \(\lambda I\); \(\mathcal J\) is finite; and a finite union of compact intervals with Borel endpoints is a measurable random compact set.  Thus both estimators and the coverage event used above are well defined.  The proof uses the eighth-moment and treatment-loading restrictions, the spectral bounds, and the fixed compact moment map, but nowhere uses a bound on \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).
